historical_record.description: The Recreation and Park Commission awarded the contract to build the playground's field house to Wm. McIntosh & Son at $25,404, from four bids, under the 1947 recreation bond program.
The Mayor approved a schedule dedicating six new playgrounds of the 1947 recreation bond program, with West Portal Playground set for June 1.
The Recreation Commission engaged William G. Merchant, architect, to design a clubhouse at West Portal Playground, on an estimated cost of $20,000.

Jack Barron of the Transit Task Force showed the Recreation and Park Commission a schematic plan reshaping West Portal Playground around the proposed Muni West Portal station, with a new building on the playground's upper terrace to replace the existing one.
Rebuilt with its recreation center because of work on the Twin Peaks Tunnel, and finished in September, West Portal Playground was rededicated on October 26, 1979.
The Recreation and Park Commission approved Open Space-funded conceptual plans for a new children's play area at West Portal Playground, with a tot area, swings and a ramp for disabled access.
The Recreation and Park Commission awarded A & R Construction a $206,835 contract to renovate the children's play area at West Portal Playground.

The Recreation Commission declined the West Portal P.T.A.'s request to rename the playground the Charlotte Estes Playground, keeping its policy against renaming established playgrounds, and suggested an inscribed sundial or drinking fountain in her memory instead.
A sundial given by the West Portal P.T.A. in memory of Charlotte Estes was dedicated at the playground on Sunday, November 15, 1942.
